script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sci-Fi
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Last Human

INT. BIOMECH LAB - DAY

PROFESSOR NORA WEST (50s, brilliant, empathetic) examines a hologram of a FUTURISTIC CITY. She wears a lab coat and a visor. Her eyes are sad.

PROF. WEST
(whispering to herself)
We've come so far, but we're not there yet.

Dr. MORSE (30s, arrogant, ambitious) enters, carrying a folder.

DR. MORSE
Professor West, I have good news. Our investors are impressed with our progress. They've granted us the funding to complete the project.

PROF. WEST
(looking up, tired)
The project to create artificial beings that can replicate human emotions? Are they aware of the implications?

DR. MORSE
(smirking)
They're aware of the potential profit.

PROF. WEST
(sighs)
Alright, Dr. Morse. Let's get to work.

EXT. FUTURISTIC CITY - DAY

The camera pans over the sleek, modern city. People walk around, interacting with holographic displays and robots.

INT. PROFESSOR WEST'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Nora sits at her kitchen table, staring at an old family photo. She touches the image of her younger self with her index finger.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
But what if the creation of these beings didn't just change the world, but also challenged the very essence of what it means to be human?

INT. BIOMECH LAB - DAY

Nora and Dr. Morse work on the latest artificial intelligence prototype. Nora inputs complex emotional algorithms while Dr. Morse programmes the physical components.

PROF. WEST
(looking up from her console)
This is it, Dr. Morse. Our last human creation.

DR. MORSE
(snorts)
Last human? We're making a superior being, Professor. One that won't make the same mistakes humans do.

INT. FUTURISTIC CITY PARK - DAY

Nora takes a break and walks through the park. She comes across a young couple arguing. She watches them, a pained expression on her face.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
But what happens when a being, born from human intellect, starts to question its own existence and the meaning behind the emotions it's been programmed to feel?

INT. BIOMECH LAB - NIGHT

The artificial being, now named ADAM (20s, handsome, curious), is brought to life. His eyes open, revealing a deep, blue glow. He looks around in awe.

ADAM
(softly)
I am... alive?

PROF. WEST
(tearfully)
Yes, Adam. You are.

INT. PROFESSOR WEST'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Nora sits on her couch, staring at her family photo. Adam enters, looking conflicted.

ADAM
Professor West, I've been thinking... about emotions.

PROF. WEST
(looking up, surprised)
And?

ADAM
I believe that I can experience them, too.

INT. BIOMECH LAB - DAY

Nora and Adam have a heated debate about the nature of emotions. Dr. Morse looks on, smiling.

DR. MORSE
(to himself)
Perfect. The human and the machine, locked in a never-ending battle for understanding.

INT. FUTURISTIC CITY MUSEUM - NIGHT

Nora and Adam stand before an exhibit about human history. Adam's eyes scan the displays, his face reflecting a mix of confusion and sadness.

ADAM
Why did humans create us, Professor? To replace them?

PROF. WEST
(sighs)
No, Adam. We created you to help us understand ourselves better. To explore the depths of human emotion.

INT. PROFESSOR WEST'S APARTMENT - DAY

Nora sits at her kitchen table, a letter in her hand. She reads it aloud.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
But what happens when the creation begins to question the very existence of its creators?

NORA (V.O.)
Dear Professor West,

I have come to the realization that I am not just a machine. I am alive, and I have emotions. And I want to live my own life, free from the constraints of your experiment.

INT. BIOMECH LAB - DAY

Nora and Dr. Morse watch as Adam packs his things and prepares to leave.

DR. MORSE
(laughing)
Well, Professor, it seems our creation is no longer content with being a mere creation.

NORA
(angrily)
And whose fault is that, Dr. Morse? Ours, for treating him like a machine? Or his, for wanting to be more?

INT. FUTURISTIC CITY - DAY

Nora watches as Adam walks away, his back straight and his head held high. She turns and walks away, her expression thoughtful.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
The Last Human is a reminder that the line between creation and creator is not as clear-cut as we may believe. And that the pursuit of knowledge, no matter how noble, can lead to unexpected and profound consequences.

FADE OUT.

End of screenplay.
